A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T1 research work. All 27 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original imputation experiments across 11 datasets, component ablations, attention analyses, efficiency measurements, and appendix sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, and supplementary experiments in Appendices B–F.

M1.justification: The mask-aware embedding, convolutional QKV projection, one-to-one channel-head binding, feed-forward network, reconstruction procedure, and training objective are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine complete benchmarks plus PhysioNet2012 and AQI36. Point, block, natural-missing, and targeted masking scenarios remain identical, including the appendix case studies.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within each experiment, including Tables 1–4, the SSSD comparison in Appendix D.3, and the PhysioNet2012 comparisons in Appendix E. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, masking protocols, sequence lengths, model configurations, training budgets, and MSE/MAE evaluation procedures match. Appendix sensitivity and controlled-attention experiments also retain their settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations, attention analyses, efficiency comparisons, hyperparameter and training-mask sensitivity studies, head-scaling experiments, and PhysioNet2012 case study.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2.2 specifies the same five random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Appendix F retains the same standard-deviation tables, with no additional uncertainty estimation or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains average MSE values of 0.027 for T1 and 0.050 for PatchTST; the detailed results and standard deviations in Tables 17–20 also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, architecture equations, kernel-scaling rule, loss formulation, and Appendix B complexity argument are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: channel-head binding, performance across 11 datasets, 46% average MSE reduction, and generalization to unseen missing patterns.

C2.justification: Interpretations of selective information transfer, attention responses, efficiency, and hyperparameter robustness are unchanged. Appendix D.2 retains the same qualification about degradation under extreme training–test masking mismatch.

D1.justification: The code-access link and implementation disclosures remain identical, including model kernels, hardware, optimizer, learning rates, batch size, early stopping, and baseline configuration procedures in Appendix A.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to CNNs, Transformers, and other imputation approaches are unchanged. The added conference-publication header is a publication-status edit.

P1.justification: v4 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', updates the arXiv version/date, and removes '(revised)' from the captions of Figures 1 and 2. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The conference header changes page presentation, and Figures 1 and 2 lose their caption revision markers. Figure artwork, table structure and highlighting, axes, legends, and placement otherwise match.

improvement.justification: v4 makes cosmetic publication and caption edits while retaining the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information throughout the appendices. Removing two revision markers provides slight polish but does not meaningfully change the paper's clarity, rigor, or usefulness.
